en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of them are actually inhabited by people.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo lowered the mountain's peak height by almost 300 meters.
Palawan's Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is a massive underground river that flows directly out into the ocean.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the steep mountains of Ifugao over 2,000 years ago entirely by hand.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second largest lake in the Philippines and is home to 18 endemic fish species.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the third deepest oceanic point on Earth.
The Philippines sits directly on the Pacific typhoon belt, causing it to experience an average of 20 tropical cyclones yearly.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry summer.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park contains the largest coral reef system in the Philippines, spanning nearly 100,000 hectares.
Cebu is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 200 kilometers from its northern to southern tips.
The Philippines holds the second-largest nickel reserves in the world, making it a top global exporter of the metal.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features incredibly clear, deep blue water that flows from an underwater cave.
